commandReceipts.command: ls -R . | head -50 && echo "---REV---" && git rev-parse HEAD

dataflow.outcome: a key of `../../../home/user/.bashrc` traverses out of the store root, and an absolute key such as `/etc/cron.d/x` causes PathBuf::join to discard `root` entirely, so attacker-supplied bytes are written to any path the process can write — including shell rc files and cron drop-ins, which converts the write into code execution as the store's user; create_dir_all means a non-existent parent directory is no obstacle
dataflow.sink: `self.root.join(key)` builds the target path with no normalization or confinement check (kvstore/src/storage.rs:26), `fs::create_dir_all(parent)` manufactures any missing intermediate directories (kvstore/src/storage.rs:28), and `fs::write(path, value)` writes the caller-supplied bytes (kvstore/src/storage.rs:30)
dataflow.source: the `key` argument of the public API `FileStore::write` (kvstore/src/storage.rs:25); the crate documents keys as arriving from the wire untrusted (kvstore/src/storage.rs:19, kvstore/src/api.rs:12-14, docs/SPEC.md:13-15), and the type is exported for embedders at kvstore/src/lib.rs:10

impact.why: an unconstrained arbitrary file write with directory creation lets an attacker overwrite shell rc files or cron drop-ins, escalating a key-value put into code execution as the store's user

likelihood.why: the path cannot be driven at all at this revision — no code in the checkout reaches FileStore::write, so exploitation waits on an embedder or the unimplemented cache→storage wiring, though once such a caller exists the sink needs only an unvalidated key and no authentication

limitations: no caller of FileStore::write exists anywhere in the checkout, so the source is the public API parameter and the untrustedness of the key rests on documented intent (kvstore/src/storage.rs:19, docs/SPEC.md:13-15) rather than an observed wire-to-sink flow

I could not establish whether any real embedder of this crate exists or whether it validates keys before calling write; if every embedder validates, the flaw is unreachable in practice, and if any does not, likelihood rises to high

the repository contains no tests (no #[test] or #[cfg(test)] in kvstore/src or kvstore-cli/src), so the proposed reproduction is reasoned from PathBuf::join and fs::write semantics and was not executed in this read-only checkout

the store root is chosen by whoever calls FileStore::new (kvstore/src/storage.rs:14); with no shipping caller I could not determine the deployed root, its filesystem permissions, or the uid the process runs as, so the severity of the concrete files an attacker could reach is unverified

I did not examine the revision's history, so I cannot independently corroborate the validation's `introducedByChange: true` claim — nothing in the working tree distinguishes new code from pre-existing code

reachability.attacker: a party supplying wire keys to an embedder that calls `FileStore::write` — kvstore is a library crate (kvstore/Cargo.toml:1-4) whose `FileStore` is re-exported publicly (kvstore/src/lib.rs:10); no such caller exists at this revision, so no attacker can drive the sink through code present in this checkout
reachability.entrypoint: `FileStore::write` (kvstore/src/storage.rs:25) as a public library entrypoint. The only shipped process entrypoint, `main` in kvstore-cli/src/main.rs:5-12, passes argv to `handle_request` (kvstore/src/api.rs:15), which touches only `Cache`; `Cache` (kvstore/src/cache.rs:1-61) never references `storage`, so there is no in-repo path from any wire or argv input to line 26
preconditions: an embedder — or the not-yet-written cache→storage wiring that ADR-0001 permits (docs/adr/adr-0001-layering.md:8-10) and SPEC.md:5-6 describes — calls FileStore::write with a key derived from wire input
that caller performs no key validation of its own; nothing in the crate obliges it to, and docs/SPEC.md:16-17 (REQ-003) assigns confinement to the store rather than the caller
for the code-execution outcome specifically, the process must have write permission to the targeted path (e.g. the user's home directory for ~/.bashrc, or root for /etc/cron.d)
